```{r matched-prose, results='asis'}
  "cost. **On what it costs to run a car, the powertrain ranking in Denmark in 2026 is ",
  "stable in the odometer and does not depend on price at all.**\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "> **What this deliberately leaves out.** Everything to do with capital: purchase price, ",
  "depreciation and the return that money would otherwise earn. Those are the larger numbers, ",
  "they run the other way, and section 8 puts them back. Read this section as *what a ",
  "kilometre costs*, not as *which car to buy*.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "> **And a caveat on the medians.** With ", nrow(cars),
  " cars across four powertrains there are only three or four of each, so the median is not ",
  "a robust central estimate. The petrol median here is ",
  fmt_num(median(cars$wltp_l_100km[cars$fuel == "benzin"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  " l/100km, pulled towards the thirsty used all-wheel-drive SUVs and away from the ",
  cars$name[cars$id == params$ref_petrol], " at ",
  fmt_num(cars$wltp_l_100km[cars$id == params$ref_petrol]),
  " - which widens the gap shown above. Section 8.4 uses one *named* car per powertrain ",
  "instead, which is both the conservative choice and the attributable one.\n"
))
```

## 8. Total cost of ownership, and the break-even cash price

Everything so far held the car fixed and asked what a kilometre costs. That question has no trade-off in it, and the electric cars won it outright. This section puts the purchase price back, and the trade-off appears immediately - because a `r fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk)` DKK car has to earn back roughly `r fmt_dkk(ev$fixed_dkk_aar)` DKK a year in "ejerafgift", insurance, calendar depreciation and foregone return before its cheaper kilometres count for anything, and at `r fmt_km(KM)` km/yr that is `r fmt_num(ev$fixed_dkk_km)` DKK/km of fixed cost against `r fmt_num(ev$marginal_dkk_km)` DKK/km of marginal cost. **The fixed side is the larger number.**

Total cost per kilometre at annual distance `d` is

$$c(d) \;=\; \underbrace{\frac{\text{"ejerafgift"} + \text{insurance} + \text{calendar depreciation} + \text{cost of capital}}{d}}_{\text{falls as } 1/d} \;+\; \underbrace{m(d)}_{\text{roughly flat}}$$

The first term is a hyperbola and the second is nearly a constant, so every car is a curve that falls steeply and then flattens. **The car with the lowest marginal cost wins only in the limit of infinite distance.** At any finite distance the curves cross.

### 8.1 What a year costs regardless of distance

```{r fixed-table}
res_c |>
  arrange(fixed_dkk_aar) |>
  transmute(
    Car = name,
    Price = fmt_dkk(price_dkk),
    `"Ejerafgift"` = fmt_dkk(ejerafgift_dkk_aar),
    Insurance = fmt_dkk(insurance_dkk_aar),
    `Calendar dep.` = fmt_dkk(dep_calendar_aar),
    Capital = fmt_dkk(capital_aar),
    `Fixed, DKK/yr` = fmt_dkk(fixed_dkk_aar)
  ) |>
  show_table(
    align = "lrrrrrr",
    caption = paste0("Annual costs that distance does not cause, over a ", YRS, "-year hold")
  )
```

### 8.2 The break-even distance between these `r nrow(cars)` cars

```{r total-curves, fig.height=7}
# Starting at 8,000 rather than lower keeps the 1/d term from stretching the y
# axis over a region no private owner drives in, which flattens everything else.
grid_km <- seq(8000, 45000, by = 500)
curves <- map_dfr(grid_km, \(d) cost_per_km(cars, sc_c, d, YRS) |>
  transmute(km_aar = d, id, name, fuel, total_dkk_km, marginal_dkk_km))

# Label each car at the right-hand edge, and mark the cheapest car at each
# distance so the switching points are visible rather than inferred.
winners <- curves |>
  group_by(km_aar) |>
  slice_min(total_dkk_km, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(curves, aes(km_aar, total_dkk_km, group = name, colour = fuel)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.65, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_line(
    data = curves |> filter(id == params$ref_ev),
    linewidth = 1.5
  ) +
  geom_point(data = winners, size = 1.5, colour = "black") +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = curves |> filter(km_aar == max(grid_km)),
    aes(label = name), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 1200, direction = "y",
    size = 2.85, seed = 2, segment.colour = "grey75", min.segment.length = 0,
    max.overlaps = Inf, box.padding = 0.16, force = 3
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = KM, linetype = "22", colour = "grey45") +
  annotate("text",
    x = KM, y = max(curves$total_dkk_km) * 0.97, hjust = -0.08,
    size = 3.1, colour = "grey35", label = paste0("your ", fmt_km(KM), " km/yr")
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_fuel, labels = lab_fuel, breaks = names(pal_fuel)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = label_comma(), breaks = seq(10000, 45000, 10000),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.42))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Total cost per kilometre, and why distance decides",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Marginal cost plus all fixed costs, over an ", YRS, "-year hold. ",
      "The bZ4X Touring is drawn heavy; black dots\nmark the cheapest car in the fleet at each distance."
    ),
    x = "Annual distance (km)", y = "DKK per km, all-in",
    caption = paste0(
      "Central setting. ", sum(cars$price_sourced), " of ", nrow(cars),
      " car prices come from listings or price lists - see section 1.1."
    )
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

```{r breakeven-table}
be <- cars |>
  filter(id != params$ref_ev) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    d_star = break_even_km(cars, sc_c, params$ref_ev, id, YRS),
    gap_at_my_km = res_c$total_dkk_km[res_c$id == params$ref_ev] -
      res_c$total_dkk_km[res_c$id == id]
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(gap_at_my_km)

be |>
  transmute(
    `bZ4X Touring vs` = name,
    Fuel = lab_fuel[fuel],
    Price = fmt_dkk(price_dkk),
    `Gap at ${KM} km/yr` = paste0(
      if_else(gap_at_my_km < 0, "bZ4X cheaper by ", "bZ4X dearer by "),
      fmt_ore(abs(gap_at_my_km)), "/km"
    ),
    `Break-even distance` = if_else(
      is.na(d_star), "never crosses",
      paste0(fmt_km(d_star), " km/yr")
    )
  ) |>
  rename_with(\(x) str_replace(x, fixed("${KM}"), fmt_km(KM))) |>
  show_table(align = "llrrr")
```

```{r breakeven-prose, results='asis'}
crosses <- be |> filter(!is.na(d_star))
never <- be |> filter(is.na(d_star))

cat(paste0(
  "At ", fmt_km(KM), " km/yr the bZ4X Touring is cheaper all-in than ",
  sum(be$gap_at_my_km < 0), " of the ", nrow(be), " comparators and dearer than ",
  sum(be$gap_at_my_km > 0), ". "
))

if (nrow(crosses) > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "Against ", nrow(crosses), " of them there is a genuine break-even distance, ",
    "ranging from ", fmt_km(min(crosses$d_star)), " to ", fmt_km(max(crosses$d_star)),
    " km/yr: drive more than that and the bZ4X's cheaper kilometres have paid for its price. "
  ))
}
if (nrow(never) > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "Against the remaining ", nrow(never),
    " the curves never cross inside 2,000 to 80,000 km/yr - one car simply dominates ",
    "the other at every distance a private owner would drive, and no amount of driving fixes it."
  ))
}
cat("\n\n")

cheapest_total <- res_c |> slice_min(total_dkk_km, n = 1)

cat(paste0(
  "**Holding the car fixed, the cheapest fuel wins and there is nothing to weigh** - ",
  "the electric cars took the top ", n_lead_el, " places in section 4. Allowing the car to ",
  "vary across a ", fmt_dkk(min(cars$price_dkk)), " to ", fmt_dkk(max(cars$price_dkk)),
  " DKK range turns it into a capital-versus-running-cost problem, and the cheapest car ",
  "all-in at ", fmt_km(KM), " km/yr becomes the **", cheapest_total$name, "** at ",
  fmt_num(cheapest_total$total_dkk_km), " DKK/km",
  if (cheapest_total$id == params$ref_ev) {
    " - which is the bZ4X itself, so on these numbers the two questions happen to agree"
  } else {
    paste0(
      ", against ", fmt_num(ev$total_dkk_km), " for the bZ4X. The question stops being ",
      "*which fuel is cheapest* and becomes *how far do I drive, and is that far enough ",
      "to amortise the price difference*"
    )
  }, ".\n"
))
```

### 8.3 Average annual cost over `r YRS` years, by fuel type

The break-even distances above still compare `r nrow(cars)` particular cars. Applying the section 7 device - a representative car per fuel type, all at the same odometer - and sweeping the cash price turns the comparison into the one a buyer actually faces: *what may this car cost, given what it will cost to run?*

```{r tco-price-sweep, fig.height=5.6}
price_grid <- seq(50000, 520000, by = 5000)

sweep_price <- expand_grid(
  fuel = fuels, odo = p(params$price_panel_odo), price = price_grid
) |>
  pmap_dfr(function(fuel, odo, price) {
    ry <- max(2011, min(2026, 2026 - round(odo / 20000)))
    car <- representative_car(cars, fuel,
      price_dkk = price, odo_km = odo, reg_year = ry,
      spec_from = if (fuel == "el") params$ref_ev else unname(spec_car[fuel])
    )
    cost_per_km(car, sc_c, KM, YRS) |>
      transmute(fuel, odo, price, total_dkk_aar)
  }) |>
  mutate(panel = paste0("Bought at ", fmt_km(odo), " km"))

panel_levels <- paste0("Bought at ", fmt_km(p(params$price_panel_odo)), " km")

ggplot(
  sweep_price |> mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_levels)),
  aes(price, total_dkk_aar, colour = fuel)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_point(
    data = tibble(
      panel = factor(panel_levels[1], levels = panel_levels),
      price = ev$price_dkk, total_dkk_aar = ev$total_dkk_aar, fuel = "el"
    ),
    size = 3, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_fuel, labels = lab_fuel, breaks = names(pal_fuel)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k")) +
  facet_wrap(~panel) +
  labs(
    title = "Total annual cost against cash price, by powertrain",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Everything included: energy, tyres, service, consumables, repair hazard, periodiske\n",
      "afgifter, insurance, depreciation and the cost of the capital. ",
      fmt_km(KM), " km/yr over ", YRS, " years.\nThe open circle is the actual bZ4X Touring."
    ),
    x = "Cash price (DKK thousand)", y = "Total cost (DKK thousand per year)",
    caption = paste0(
      "Each line is one named car per powertrain - the reference cars in section 1.1 - with only its ",
      "price varying.\nThat is a ceteris paribus device: in the real market a cheaper car is usually ",
      "also a thirstier one."
    )
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

The lines are close to parallel, and that is the substantive point. The **slope** is what a krone of purchase price costs per year - depreciation plus foregone return, around `r fmt_pct((sweep_price$total_dkk_aar[sweep_price$fuel == "el" & sweep_price$odo == 0 & sweep_price$price == 400000] - sweep_price$total_dkk_aar[sweep_price$fuel == "el" & sweep_price$odo == 0 & sweep_price$price == 200000]) / 200000, 1)` a year for an electric car - and it barely differs between powertrains. The **vertical gaps between the lines** are the running-cost differences from section 7. Dividing one by the other gives the number the decision turns on.

### 8.4 The break-even cash price

> **How much may an electric car cost and still be no more expensive to own than a combustion one?**

```{r break-even-price-table}
be_price <- expand_grid(fuel = setdiff(fuels, "el"), odo = p(params$price_panel_odo)) |>
  pmap_dfr(function(fuel, odo) {
    ry <- max(2011, min(2026, 2026 - round(odo / 20000)))
    # The electric side is anchored at the reference car's price and specs; the
    # comparator's price is what gets solved for.
    ev_car <- representative_car(cars, "el",
      price_dkk = ev$price_dkk, odo_km = odo, reg_year = ry,
      spec_from = params$ref_ev
    )
    target <- cost_per_km(ev_car, sc_c, KM, YRS)$total_dkk_aar
    comp <- representative_car(cars, fuel,
      price_dkk = 200000, odo_km = odo, reg_year = ry,
      spec_from = unname(spec_car[fuel])
    )
    tibble(
      fuel = fuel, odo = odo, target = target,
      p_star = break_even_price(target, comp, sc_c, KM, YRS)
    )
  })

be_price |>
  transmute(
    Fuel = lab_fuel[fuel],
    odo = paste0("At ", fmt_km(odo), " km"),
    v = if_else(is.na(p_star), "no crossing", fmt_dkk(p_star))
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = odo, values_from = v) |>
  show_table(
    align = "lrrr",
    caption = paste0(
      "Cash price at which a combustion car matches an electric one bought for ",
      fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk), " DKK, on total annual cost"
    )
  )
```

```{r break-even-price-prose, results='asis'}
b0 <- be_price |> filter(odo == 0, !is.na(p_star))

if (nrow(b0) == 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "At zero kilometres no combustion price inside the search bracket equalises the two, ",
    "which means the electric car's running-cost advantage cannot be bought back at any ",
    "purchase price a private buyer would pay.\n"
  ))
} else {
  # Petrol is the mainstream comparator, so it anchors the headline; the plug-in
  # hybrid gives the tightest bound and is reported as the conservative case.
  pe_row <- b0 |> filter(fuel == "benzin")
  tightest <- b0 |> slice_max(p_star, n = 1)

  cat(paste0(
    "**A new electric car bought for ", fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk),
    " DKK costs the same per year to own as a petrol car bought for ",
    fmt_dkk(pe_row$p_star), " DKK.** The electric car may therefore cost **",
    fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk - pe_row$p_star), " DKK more** at the till and still break even ",
    "over ", YRS, " years at ", fmt_km(KM), " km. Against the other powertrains the ",
    "allowance is ",
    paste0(
      b0 |> filter(fuel != "benzin") |>
        mutate(s = paste0(fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk - p_star), " DKK vs ", tolower(lab_fuel[fuel]))) |>
        pull(s),
      collapse = " and "
    ), ".\n\n"
  ))

  cat(paste0(
    "Read the other way it is a rule of thumb worth carrying into a showroom: at ",
    fmt_km(KM), " km/yr an electric car is worth **",
    fmt_dkk(round((ev$price_dkk - pe_row$p_star) / 10000) * 10000),
    " DKK more than an equivalent petrol car**, and at least **",
    fmt_dkk(round((ev$price_dkk - tightest$p_star) / 10000) * 10000),
    " DKK more** than the closest-run alternative in the fleet, the ",
    tolower(lab_fuel[tightest$fuel]), ". Below that premium it wins on total cost; ",
    "above it, the cheaper kilometres do not repay the capital.\n\n"
  ))

  # The break-even price is only meaningful if a car can actually be bought for
  # it. When it falls below the whole new-car market, the finding is stronger
  # than a premium: it is a dominance result.
  new_ice <- cars |> filter(condition == "ny", fuel %in% c("benzin", "diesel"))
  if (nrow(new_ice) > 0 && pe_row$p_star < min(new_ice$price_dkk)) {
    cat(paste0(
      "**", fmt_dkk(pe_row$p_star),
      " DKK is below the cheapest new combustion car in the fleet** (",
      new_ice$name[which.min(new_ice$price_dkk)], " at ",
      fmt_dkk(min(new_ice$price_dkk)), " DKK), and well below anything of this size ",
      "on sale. So at ", fmt_km(KM), " km/yr the comparison against *new* combustion ",
      "cars is not a premium at all - it is a dominance result: no new petrol or diesel ",
      "wagon in this class can be bought cheaply enough to match the electric car on ",
      "total cost. The real competition is the used market, which is what the ",
      fmt_km(100000), " and ", fmt_km(200000), " km columns above are for.\n\n"
    ))
  }
}

# Sensitivity of the premium to annual distance: the one variable the buyer controls.
prem_by_km <- map_dfr(c(10000, 15000, 20000, 30000, 40000), function(d) {
  ev_car <- representative_car(cars, "el",
    price_dkk = ev$price_dkk, odo_km = 0, reg_year = 2026, spec_from = params$ref_ev
  )
  target <- cost_per_km(ev_car, sc_c, d, YRS)$total_dkk_aar
  comp <- representative_car(cars, "benzin",
    price_dkk = 200000, odo_km = 0, reg_year = 2026, spec_from = params$ref_petrol
  )
  tibble(km = d, p_star = break_even_price(target, comp, sc_c, d, YRS))
}) |>
  mutate(premium = ev$price_dkk - p_star)

cat("The premium is not a constant - it scales with how far you drive, because that is what turns a per-kilometre advantage into kroner:\n\n")
```

```{r premium-by-distance}
prem_by_km |>
  transmute(
    `Annual distance` = paste0(fmt_km(km), " km"),
    `Break-even petrol price` = if_else(is.na(p_star),
      "none exists", fmt_dkk(p_star)
    ),
    `Electric premium justified` = if_else(is.na(premium),
      "any price wins", fmt_dkk(premium)
    )
  ) |>
  show_table(align = "lrr")
```

```{r premium-nocross, results='asis'}
nocross <- prem_by_km |> filter(is.na(p_star))
if (nrow(nocross) > 0) {
  cat(paste0(
    "The rows marked *none exists* are not a failure of the solver. Above about ",
    fmt_km(min(nocross$km)), " km/yr the electric car is cheaper per year than a petrol ",
    "car at **any** purchase price down to the ", fmt_dkk(20000),
    " DKK floor of the search - the running-cost gap over ", YRS,
    " years exceeds the entire value of a cheap petrol car, so no discount closes it.\n"
  ))
}
```

```{r premium-caveat, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  "> **Three caveats before using this number.** The comparator is the ",
  cars$name[cars$id == params$ref_petrol], " at its published ",
  fmt_num(cars$wltp_l_100km[cars$id == params$ref_petrol]),
  " l/100km, with only its price varying. That is the most efficient all-wheel-drive petrol ",
  "car in the fleet, so this is the conservative comparison - against any of the AWD petrol ",
  "SUVs at 8 to 9 l/100km the justified premium would be substantially larger. The prices ",
  "behind the comparators are placeholders for every car except ",
  knitr::combine_words(cars$name[cars$price_sourced]), ". And roughly ",
  fmt_pct((pe$c_dep_km - ev$c_dep_km) / (pe$marginal_dkk_km - ev$marginal_dkk_km)),
  " of the per-kilometre gap rests on the electric depreciation elasticity from section 5.4, ",
  "whose sign depends on the regression controls - section 9.2 shows what halving it does.\n"
))
```

## 9. Sensitivity

### 9.1 Both prices at once

```{r heatmap, fig.height=5.4}
pet_grid <- seq(12, 24, length.out = 80)
# The electricity axis runs past the top of the ad-hoc DC range on purpose: the
# break-even sits above every price actually charged in Denmark, and a grid that
# stopped at the market price would hide the contour rather than show it.
el_grid <- seq(0.5, 9.0, length.out = 80)

# Energy cost per km only: the other components do not move with these two
# prices, so including them would just add a constant and shift the contour.
hm <- expand_grid(petrol = pet_grid, el = el_grid) |>
  mutate(
    ev_energy = ev$use_wh_km / 1000 * el,
    pe_energy = pe$use_l_100 / 100 * petrol,
    # Constant offset from everything that is not energy, so the zero contour
    # is the total marginal break-even and not just the energy break-even.
    other = (ev$marginal_dkk_km - ev$c_energy) - (pe$marginal_dkk_km - pe$c_energy),
    diff = ev_energy - pe_energy + other
  )

ggplot(hm, aes(petrol, el)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = diff), interpolate = TRUE) +
  geom_contour(aes(z = diff), breaks = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # The dearest electricity actually on sale in Denmark. Everything below this
  # line is a price a driver can face; everything above it is hypothetical.
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = tier_price$high[["dc_adhoc"]],
    linetype = "22", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = min(pet_grid), y = tier_price$high[["dc_adhoc"]], hjust = -0.03, vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3, colour = "grey20",
    label = "dearest ad-hoc DC charging on sale in DK"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    x = sc_c$petrol_dkk_l, y = sc_c$el_dkk_kwh,
    size = 3, shape = 21, fill = "white", stroke = 1.1
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = sc_c$petrol_dkk_l, y = sc_c$el_dkk_kwh, hjust = -0.18, vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3.2, label = "today, your profile"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = pal_fuel[["el"]], mid = "grey96", high = pal_fuel[["benzin"]],
    midpoint = 0, labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "The bZ4X Touring against the new petrol wagon, on marginal cost",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Blue: the bZ4X is cheaper per km. Orange: the ", pe$name,
      " is. The black line is the\nbreak-even, including tyres, service, consumables ",
      "and depreciation, not just energy."
    ),
    x = "Petrol, DKK per litre", y = "Blended electricity, DKK per kWh",
    fill = "DKK/km"
  ) +
  theme_note() +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(colour = "grey30"))
```

```{r heatmap-prose, results='asis'}
at_today <- hm |>
  filter(abs(petrol - sc_c$petrol_dkk_l) == min(abs(petrol - sc_c$petrol_dkk_l)))
crossing <- at_today |>
  filter(diff >= 0) |>
  slice_min(el, n = 1)

cat(paste0(
  "The break-even line is nearly flat, and it sits high. At today's petrol price of ",
  fmt_num(sc_c$petrol_dkk_l), " DKK/l, electricity would have to reach ",
  if (nrow(crossing) == 0) {
    paste0("more than ", fmt_num(max(el_grid)), " DKK/kWh - beyond the top of the grid")
  } else {
    paste0(fmt_num(crossing$el[1]), " DKK/kWh")
  },
  " before the bZ4X's total marginal cost exceeded the petrol wagon's. The dearest ",
  "electricity a Danish driver can realistically buy is ad-hoc DC at ",
  fmt_num(tier_price$high[["dc_adhoc"]]), " DKK/kWh, and the flatness of the contour ",
  "says why the margin is so wide: the two cars differ by ",
  fmt_ore(abs((ev$marginal_dkk_km - ev$c_energy) - (pe$marginal_dkk_km - pe$c_energy))),
  "/km on everything that is not energy, and that difference already favours the ",
  "electric car before a single kilowatt-hour is priced.\n"
))
```

### 9.2 The depreciation elasticities

Section 5.4 showed the electric elasticity flipping sign under a change of controls. Scaling all three by a common factor puts a bound on what that fragility can do.

```{r elast-sens}
map_dfr(p(params$e_km_scale_sensitivity), function(s) {
  sc <- sc_c
  sc$e_km_scale <- s
  cost_per_km(cars, sc, KM, YRS) |> mutate(scale = s)
}) |>
  filter(id %in% c(params$ref_ev, params$ref_petrol, params$ref_diesel, best_marg$id)) |>
  transmute(scale = paste0("x ", fmt_num(scale, 1)), name, v = fmt_num(marginal_dkk_km)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = scale, values_from = v) |>
  rename(Car = name) |>
  show_table(align = "lrrr")
```

### 9.3 When the "elafgift" cut expires

The 2026-27 electricity tax cut is temporary. If the rate returns to its 2025 level of 90 oere/kWh before VAT, home charging rises by about `r fmt_num(0.90 * 1.25)` DKK/kWh.

```{r elafgift-expiry, results='asis'}
restore <- 0.90 * 1.25 # 2025 rate plus VAT
mix_home <- my_mix
# Only the two home tiers carry the household elafgift; public charge point
# operators are on a different (refunded) footing, so their prices move less.
tiers_after <- tier_price$central
tiers_after[["home_night"]] <- tiers_after[["home_night"]] + restore
tiers_after[["home_avg"]] <- tiers_after[["home_avg"]] + restore

sc_after <- sc_c
sc_after$el_dkk_kwh <- blend_el(mix_home, tiers_after)
after <- cost_per_km(cars, sc_after, KM, YRS)
ev_after <- after$marginal_dkk_km[after$id == params$ref_ev]

cat(paste0(
  "On your profile the blended price would go from ", fmt_num(sc_c$el_dkk_kwh),
  " to ", fmt_num(sc_after$el_dkk_kwh), " DKK/kWh, and the bZ4X's marginal cost from ",
  fmt_num(ev$marginal_dkk_km), " to ", fmt_num(ev_after), " DKK/km - a rise of ",
  fmt_ore(ev_after - ev$marginal_dkk_km), "/km, or ",
  fmt_dkk((ev_after - ev$marginal_dkk_km) * KM), " DKK a year at ", fmt_km(KM), " km. ",
  "The electric car is ",
  if (ev_after < pe$marginal_dkk_km) {
    paste0(
      "still cheaper per kilometre than the ", pe$name, ", by ",
      fmt_ore(pe$marginal_dkk_km - ev_after), "/km. The cut is worth having but the ",
      "conclusion does not depend on it."
    )
  } else {
    paste0(
      "then more expensive per kilometre than the ", pe$name, ", by ",
      fmt_ore(ev_after - pe$marginal_dkk_km), "/km. The 2026 conclusion depends on a ",
      "temporary tax measure, which is worth knowing before signing an eight-year plan."
    )
  }, "\n"
))
```

### 9.4 How far would petrol have to fall?

Section 2.4 widened the fuel bands because today's prices are near records and an eight-year hold is exposed to them coming back down. This section asks what that would actually do, by moving the pump price alone and leaving electricity where it is - the decorrelated case the bands cannot show.

```{r petrol-fall, fig.height=5}
fall_grid <- seq(9, 24, by = 0.25)

fall <- map_dfr(fall_grid, function(pp) {
  sc <- sc_c
  sc$petrol_dkk_l <- pp
  sc$diesel_dkk_l <- pp + (sc_c$diesel_dkk_l - sc_c$petrol_dkk_l)

  ev_car <- representative_car(cars, "el",
    price_dkk = ev$price_dkk, odo_km = 0, reg_year = 2026, spec_from = params$ref_ev
  )
  target <- cost_per_km(ev_car, sc, KM, YRS)$total_dkk_aar
  comp <- representative_car(cars, "benzin",
    price_dkk = 200000, odo_km = 0, reg_year = 2026, spec_from = params$ref_petrol
  )

  x <- cost_per_km(cars, sc, KM, YRS)
  tibble(
    petrol = pp,
    marg_gap = x$marginal_dkk_km[x$id == params$ref_petrol] -
      x$marginal_dkk_km[x$id == params$ref_ev],
    premium = ev$price_dkk - break_even_price(target, comp, sc, KM, YRS)
  )
})

hist_band <- range(price_hist$dkk[price_hist$series == "petrol" & price_hist$basis == "street"])

ggplot(fall, aes(petrol, premium)) +
  annotate("rect",
    xmin = hist_band[1], xmax = hist_band[2], ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "grey85", alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  annotate("text",
    x = mean(hist_band), y = max(fall$premium, na.rm = TRUE), vjust = 1.4,
    size = 3.1, colour = "grey35", label = "petrol's 2020-2026 range"
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1, colour = pal_fuel[["el"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sc_c$petrol_dkk_l, linetype = "22", colour = "grey40") +
  annotate("text",
    x = sc_c$petrol_dkk_l, y = min(fall$premium, na.rm = TRUE), hjust = -0.07,
    vjust = -0.6, size = 3.1, colour = "grey30", label = "today"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k")) +
  labs(
    title = "The justified electric premium, as a function of the petrol price",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "How much more an electric car may cost than an equivalent petrol one and still break even\n",
      "over ", YRS, " years at ", fmt_km(KM),
      " km/yr. Electricity is held at today's blended ", fmt_num(sc_c$el_dkk_kwh), " DKK/kWh."
    ),
    x = "Petrol, DKK per litre", y = "Electric premium justified (DKK thousand)",
    caption = "Diesel is moved with petrol, keeping today's spread between them. Central setting otherwise."
  ) +
  theme_note()
```

```{r petrol-fall-prose, results='asis'}
at_low <- fall |> filter(abs(petrol - p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[1]) == min(abs(petrol - p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[1])))
at_hi <- fall |> filter(abs(petrol - p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[3]) == min(abs(petrol - p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[3])))
at_now <- fall |> filter(abs(petrol - sc_c$petrol_dkk_l) == min(abs(petrol - sc_c$petrol_dkk_l)))

zero_marg <- fall |> filter(marg_gap <= 0)
zero_prem <- fall |> filter(premium <= 0)

cat(paste0(
  "**The premium is roughly linear in the pump price, and the exposure is material.** ",
  "At today's ", fmt_num(sc_c$petrol_dkk_l), " DKK/l an electric car is worth ",
  fmt_dkk(at_now$premium[1]), " DKK more; at the bottom of the band (",
  fmt_num(p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[1]), " DKK/l, roughly the 2024-25 level) it is worth ",
  fmt_dkk(at_low$premium[1]), " DKK, and at the top (",
  fmt_num(p(params$petrol_dkk_l)[3]), " DKK/l) ", fmt_dkk(at_hi$premium[1]), " DKK. ",
  "So the fuel-price question moves the answer by about ",
  fmt_dkk(at_hi$premium[1] - at_low$premium[1]),
  " DKK across the credible range - which is the right order of magnitude to care about ",
  "when the car itself costs ", fmt_dkk(ev$price_dkk), " DKK.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "**But the sign does not change anywhere on the grid.** ",
  if (nrow(zero_marg) == 0) {
    paste0(
      "Down to ", fmt_num(min(fall_grid)),
      " DKK/l - below any Danish pump price this century - the petrol car still costs more per ",
      "kilometre to run than the bZ4X, and the justified premium stays positive throughout. "
    )
  } else {
    paste0(
      "The marginal ranking reverses only below ", fmt_num(max(zero_marg$petrol)),
      " DKK/l. "
    )
  },
  "That is the reassuring half of the answer: **a fall in fuel prices changes how much the ",
  "electric car is worth paying for, not whether it is worth paying more.**\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "> **The reason is structural rather than lucky.** Roughly half of a litre's pump price ",
  "in Denmark is duty and VAT - the VAT alone is a fifth of it - and the duty component is on a ",
  "legislated upward path - the CO2 rate rose in 2025, diesel's now exceeds petrol's, and ",
  "ETS2 arrives in 2027. A collapse in crude moves only the part of the price that is not tax, ",
  "so even a halving of the oil price does not halve what you pay at the pump. ",
  "The electricity side has the mirror-image asymmetry: its tax was cut to the EU minimum ",
  "for 2026-27 and can only go back up, which is what section 9.3 prices. Neither of those ",
  "is a forecast, but they do mean the two bands are not symmetric bets.\n"
))
```

### 9.5 What is deliberately not modelled

Charging time and the value of it; the convenience of a five-minute fill against a thirty-minute stop, in both directions. Battery degradation as a per-kilometre cost and the warranty that covers it - that is a whole question of its own and it is answered in `battery-warranty/warranty-analysis.Rmd`. Company-car taxation, which changes the arithmetic completely for anyone on **"fri bil"**. Registration tax changes on future purchases. Road tolls and bridge fees. Anything to do with emissions other than through the taxes already priced in.

## 10. Verdict

```{r verdict, results='asis'}
cat(paste0(
  "**On the narrow question - what a kilometre costs, holding distance equal - ",
  "electricity wins outright.** It takes the energy contest by a ",
  "factor of ", fmt_num(en_pe / en_ev, 1), " and keeps essentially all of it: the tyre ",
  "penalty from carrying ", fmt_km(ev$kerb_kg - pe$kerb_kg), " kg more is cancelled by ",
  "cheaper consumables and servicing. The bZ4X Touring's marginal cost is ",
  fmt_num(ev$marginal_dkk_km), " DKK/km against ", fmt_num(pe$marginal_dkk_km),
  " for a new petrol wagon and ", fmt_num(di$marginal_dkk_km),
  " for a used diesel, and no setting of the energy prices reverses that. There is no ",
  "trade-off to weigh at this level.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "**Holding the odometer equal rather than the car confirms it.** A representative ",
  "electric car is cheaper to run than the best combustion alternative at every odometer ",
  "from 0 to ", fmt_km(max(matched$odo)), " km, by ", fmt_ore(gap0), " to ",
  fmt_ore(gapmax), "/km, and the gap widens with age rather than closing. That comparison ",
  "contains no capital, so it cannot be an artefact of what the cars cost, and it holds ",
  "mileage constant, so it cannot be an artefact of comparing new electric cars with ",
  "worn-out diesels. The \"periodiske afgifter\" add ", fmt_ore(
    (mean(tax_di$ejerafgift_dkk_aar) - mean(tax_el$ejerafgift_dkk_aar)) / KM
  ), "/km to that gap against diesel, and are being tightened further from 2027.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "**That holds only with the car held fixed.** Across ",
  fmt_dkk(min(cars$price_dkk)), " to ", fmt_dkk(max(cars$price_dkk)),
  " DKK the marginal ranking and the total ranking are different rankings: the bZ4X ",
  "carries ", fmt_num(ev$fixed_dkk_km), " DKK/km of fixed cost at ", fmt_km(KM),
  " km/yr, more than its entire marginal cost, and the cheapest car all-in is the **",
  cheapest_total$name, "**. The decision variable stops being the fuel and becomes the ",
  "annual distance.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "**The number to take away is the break-even cash price.** At ", fmt_km(KM),
  " km/yr over ", YRS, " years an electric car is worth about **",
  fmt_dkk(round((ev$price_dkk - be_price$p_star[be_price$fuel == "benzin" & be_price$odo == 0]) / 10000) * 10000),
  " DKK more than an equivalent petrol car** and still breaks even, rising to roughly ",
  fmt_dkk(round(prem_by_km$premium[prem_by_km$km == 30000] / 10000) * 10000),
  " DKK at 30,000 km/yr. That is the form the answer takes once mileage and price are ",
  "both in play: not a fuel, but a price you are allowed to pay.\n\n"
))

cat(paste0(
  "**Three things would change the answer, in descending order of how much:** ",
  "the prices in `fuel-cost-cars.csv`, which drive section 8 entirely",
  if (any(!cars$price_sourced)) {
    paste0(
      " and which remain placeholders for ", sum(!cars$price_sourced), " of ",
      nrow(cars), " cars"
    )
  } else {
    ""
  },
  "; the repair-hazard slope, ",
  "which decides whether the cheap end of the fleet is a bargain or a trap; and the ",
  "electric depreciation elasticity, whose sign depends on the regression controls. ",
  "None of the three is a fuel price.\n\n"
))
```
